Hi Carl / Julia —

Thanks for the request. Below is a concise summary (high level) and attached evidence artifacts; I can follow with more formal attestation if needed.

1) EU-only processing and storage
- We support in-region inference and persistent storage in EU regions (Frankfurt, Paris, Amsterdam). Customers can select EU-only routing at the tenant level.
- Control plane tenancy: hosted control plane operates from EU control plane for Private customers upon request; Dedicated and Private customers may choose a customer-controlled control plane.

2) Backups & snapshots
- Backups and periodic snapshots are stored in the same region as the primary dataset by default for EU-only deployments.
- All disk and object storage are encrypted at-rest with customer managed KMS keys (optionally) or Redwood-managed keys.
- Deletion process: primary deletion request triggers TTL-based lifecycle that deletes active objects and submits asynchronous snapshot cleanup for all associated volumes and object versions. Typical completion window for end-to-end deletion (primary data + snapshots + KV caches) is 72 hours; we provide an estimate and update for longer retention holds (legal/forensic).

3) Proof of deletion and audit logs
- We can provide time-stamped audit log entries showing deletion operations, KMS key rotation logs, and object-store deletion events.
- For customers requiring cryptographic proof, we offer deletion attestations (PDF) generated after confirmation of snapshot purge. Attached: redwood-eu-sccs-evidence-pack-v1.pdf (contains sample audit extracts).

4) Operator access and entitlements
- Operator access is limited by role-based entitlements. For EU-only Private/Dedicated deployments, operator access is tightly scoped and requires documented justification, time-bounded break-glass, and multi-party approval.
- All operator sessions are recorded; administrative actions affecting customer data are logged and retained for 12 months (longer retention available as an add-on).

5) SCCs and Schrems II position
- Redwood provides SCCs (EU Standard Contractual Clauses) as the transfer mechanism. Where processing is constrained to EU-only regions and control plane is EU-hosted, transfer risk is materially reduced; however we recommend your legal team review the full SCCs and our transfer impact assessment (TIA) — excerpts included in the evidence pack.

Attachments: redwood-eu-sccs-evidence-pack-v1.pdf, sccs-implementation-checklist.xlsx

Next steps we propose:
- Sign an evidence NDA if you prefer redacted logs (we can provide a one-way NDA).
- Schedule a 30-min technical call (Marissa proposed Wed 24th at 10:00 CEST).
- If you have specific retention windows or legal holds, share them so we can map operational timelines.

If you'd like, Rishi can add a short technical appendix on KV cache eviction and inference-only ephemeral storage behavior.

Regards,
Lauren Bishop

Hi Carl / Julia — quick technical clarifications to answer Lauren's notes and your specific asks: 

- Replication & cold backups: for EU-only Dedicated/Private tenants, automated replication and cold backup copies are kept in-region by default. Cold backups that are archived to lower-cost tiers remain in-region unless you explicitly authorize cross-region archival. The deletion workflow triggers background cleanup tasks that remove object versions and snapshot references; for archived cold backups we schedule a retention purge which can take up to 7 days depending on storage tier and archive retrieval cadence. We'll include exact bucket-level deletion logs in the attestation.

- Operator break-glass: break-glass approvals produce immutable audit records. Those records include approver identity, justification, time-stamp, and revised operational scope. We can export those records as part of the attestation package (CSV + signed PDF).

- KV cache and ephemeral inference state: KV caches are ephemeral and evicted per-tenant on deletion; we do not persist cached tokens beyond the lifecycle window and do not include them in backups. If you require an explicit cache-flush before deletion we'll perform that as an operational step and record it in the deletion attestation.

I'll upload a short technical appendix and example logs to the Drive folder Lauren referenced by EOD today. If you'd like a one-page timeline mapping (request -> TTL trigger -> snapshot purge -> attestation delivery) I can produce that for procurement.

Regards,
Rishi Malhotra
Director, Serving Runtime | Redwood Inference
